$comment: CLAUDE.md §12 and docs/15-tasks.md Phase 8. Read by tools/check-dependencies.sh. A package is never added to the tolerated tier — it is either allowed under §12.2 or it does not come in.

typescript.why: The compiler. Nothing built into Node performs static type-checking, and hammer's every guarantee in CLAUDE.md §3.1 (readonly, branded types, exhaustive unions) is enforced by this program and by no other.
typescript.owner: Microsoft, a decade of stable major releases
typescript.replaces: no built-in — the platform has no static type-checker; the alternative is untyped JavaScript

esbuild.why: The measuring bundler. Nothing in the platform bundles or minifies, and the byte budgets (tools/check-bundle-budget.sh), the tree-shaking assertions (tests/codegen/built_output.test.ts) and the markup-sink scan of a shipped bundle (tests/dom/bundle.test.ts) are all claims about exactly what a consumer's bundler emits. Zero JS dependencies; its own tree is the platform binary only.
esbuild.owner: Evan Wallace, in continuous release since 2020 and the bundler most consuming applications already run
esbuild.replaces: no built-in bundler or minifier exists in Node

react.why: The peer hammer/react adapts. An adapter tested without the library it adapts is tested against a belief about that library rather than the library itself.
react.owner: Meta, a decade of stable major releases
react.replaces: not applicable — this is the peer being adapted, not a stand-in for a platform primitive

react-dom.why: The renderer half of the same peer. hammer/react's hooks are exercised against real mount and unmount lifecycles, which is where a leaked subscription or a state update after unmount actually shows up.
react-dom.owner: Meta, a decade of stable major releases
react-dom.replaces: not applicable — this is the peer being adapted, not a stand-in for a platform primitive

@types/react.why: Ambient declarations for the peer above. Nothing in the package executes; it is read by tsc and by nothing else.
@types/react.owner: the DefinitelyTyped project, published under the community's types-publisher bot
@types/react.replaces: no built-in — the platform ships no ambient types for a peer it does not itself provide

@types/react-dom.why: Ambient declarations for react-dom. Nothing in the package executes.
@types/react-dom.owner: the DefinitelyTyped project, published under the community's types-publisher bot
@types/react-dom.replaces: no built-in — the platform ships no ambient types for a peer it does not itself provide

@types/node.why: Ambient declarations for the Node APIs codegen and the tools/ scripts call (node:fs, node:path, node:crypto). Nothing in the package executes.
@types/node.owner: the DefinitelyTyped project, published under the community's types-publisher bot, tracking Node's own release line
@types/node.replaces: no built-in — Node ships no ambient TypeScript types for its own APIs

installScripts.node_modules/esbuild: postinstall downloads the platform binary; ignore-scripts disables it, and the pinned optional @esbuild/<platform> package supplies the same binary the script would have fetched
